dedupe_keys.name: fsbrick an information model for representing fault symptom relationships in heating ventilation and air conditioning systems

description: FSBrick: an information model for representing fault-symptom relationships in heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems is a data set described in the paper "FSBrick: an information model for representing fault-symptom relationships in heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems" in Data-Centric Engineering (Cambridge University Press, 2024), produced by Min Young Hwang, Burcu Akinci, Mario Bergés. Current fault diagnosis (FD) methods for heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems do not accommodate for system reconfigurations throughout the systems’ lifetime. However, system reconfiguration can change the causal relationship between faults and symptoms, which leads to a drop in FD accuracy. Coverage: building HVAC systems. The paper does not give a data set link that the open sources used could show, so the paper is the only link; the data location and formats need checking on the paper page, which the cloud cannot open for this journal. Licence: not stated (data set page not reachable on 2026-10-01; the paper is CC-BY-4.0). Cost: no charge is stated in the metadata read; the paper's own access terms were not checked. Caveats: written from the paper's abstract and metadata only, so contents, quality and current availability are unchecked and the description may lag the source. It can support fault diagnosis in building heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems. Related: the paper is the Data-Centric Engineering article 10.1017/dce.2024.26.
